title: Kakko (small laced drum)
summary: The kakko is a small barrel drum laced with cords and played with two thin sticks in the court orchestra of Japan. It sits on a low stand and its quick, dry strokes mark the start of each phrase and keep the whole ensemble to one steady tempo.
howToPlay: The drum sits on its stand with the near head toward you and the body running away to the right.
Centre is the bright middle of the head, Edge the ring round it, Rim the hoop at the top and Side the lacquered body.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the steady centre strokes, then add the edge and the rim.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: In the court orchestra the kakko player is the one who leads. A slow run of strokes that speeds up tells the other players when to come in, and a settled pulse tells them the tempo for the whole piece.
credits: Tradition: the 鞨鼓; patterns written for this game
